answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before earning trust, and a raven-like sentinel service watches for clusters of fresh identities behaving identically. Reputation flows like cargo through a wharf - it accumulates slowly from verified work and is lost instantly on fraud, so an attacker must fund many deposits and wait months to grow an orchard of credible sockpuppets, while honest agents keep compounding. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a hundred trusted ones costs more than the attack can return.
